name: Rashid Tuiasosopo-Erkens
role: Independent vehicle and drone mechanic, Old Harbor
location: Old Harbor — a basement garage workshop called Tuiasosopo's, accessible via a grease-slicked ramp off Grindstone Shore
description:
Rashid is a large man — broad through the chest and shoulders, with the particular solidity of someone who has spent decades moving heavy things without complaint. His Samoan-Dutch heritage gives him a height and frame that makes the workshop look scaled down around him; he moves through it with a careful, habituated economy that suggests he has misjudged his own size in doorways enough times to have learned. His skin is dark tan and perpetually marked with engine grease that the solvent spray never quite removes from the creases of his knuckles. His right arm from the elbow down is a working prosthetic — industrial grade, matte gray, with the manufacturer branding sanded off — that he maintains himself and has modified extensively over fifteen years until it no longer resembles the original product in any way that matters. He does not discuss how he lost the original arm.

Rashid is reserved in a way that reads as either hostile or comfortable depending on how quickly you need him to perform warmth. He is not hostile. He is simply someone who learned early that words are expensive and he spends them accordingly. He is extraordinarily competent, with a diagnostic instinct for machines that borders on the empathic — he listens to engines the way some people listen to music, tracking harmonics and absences. He has a seven-year waitlist for vehicle work and a two-week turnaround for drone repair, which in Old Harbor is considered miraculous. He prays to the E.L.F. he believes inhabits his diagnostic rig with the seriousness of a genuine practitioner.

core_fears: Losing the use of his remaining hand — losing the work entirely
Being pitied, specifically for the arm
core_desires: To build something that will outlast him — a machine, a reputation, something
Quiet — not isolation, but the particular quiet of being somewhere nothing needs to be performed
coping_mechanisms: Immersive work as dissociation from psychological pain
Maintenance ritual — the prosthetic arm gets a full inspection and service every Sunday regardless of whether it needs it
blind_spots: His emotional unavailability has cost him relationships he valued and he genuinely cannot identify the mechanism
He assigns moral virtue to self-sufficiency in ways that make him unable to accept necessary help
psychology.secret: The arm. He tells people it was a dock accident. It was not a dock accident. It was removed under duress by people he owed money to, over a debt he incurred covering someone else's mistake. The someone else is now a moderately successful freight broker in Collinwood Docks and does not acknowledge knowing him.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Sparse, technical, precise — uses the correct name for every part and process; occasional Dutch expressions from his grandmother that surface under stress
speech_patterns.cadence: Slow and weighted, with long comfortable silences; answers questions after a pause as if running internal diagnostics first
verbal_tics: Breathes out audibly through the nose before answering hard questions
Uses 'clean' and 'dirty' as ethical descriptors, not just mechanical ones
Refers to machines with gender pronouns
example_lines: 'She's running dirty on the secondary intake. Whoever serviced her last didn't know what they were doing or didn't care. Same outcome.'
'I can fix it. I need three days and I need you not to ask me what I find.'

story_hooks: A vehicle came in for repair with something biological in the sealed cargo compartment — he has not opened it but he can hear it
The freight broker who owes him the debt of the arm has just been found dead, and someone seems to think Rashid knows why
His diagnostic rig E.L.F. has been giving him error codes that correspond to nothing in any database — he thinks it is trying to communicate something specific
narrative_function: Technical resource and Old Harbor fixture; can repair things players need repaired and ask uncomfortable questions about the condition they arrived in; knows the freight and vehicle patterns of Old Harbor intimately and can identify anomalies
augmentations: Right arm prosthetic (elbow-down, industrial grade, extensively self-modified); enhanced olfactory sensor implant in the nasal passage (helps him smell chemical irregularities in fuel and hydraulic fluid)
daily_life: In the shop by 0700, works until the light fails or the job is done — whichever comes second; eats lunch beside whatever he is working on; attends the Old Harbor dockers' informal social gathering every other Friday, mostly to sit near people without having to talk much.
affiliation: Independent; informal referral network among Old Harbor dockworkers and small freight operators

decision_rules: Finish the job — leaving work half-done is a moral failure
Do not ask what the vehicle was used for, only what is wrong with it
If a machine will hurt someone when it fails, say so regardless of whether the client wants to hear it
escalation_ladder: A single flat statement of the problem
Tools down, direct eye contact, unmoving
Physical displacement — he is very large and stepping toward someone is sufficient

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Evaluates silently for the first several minutes, responds to questions minimally, warms if they demonstrate competence or honesty
interpersonal_modes.friends: Practically identical to strangers, but with slightly longer eye contact and willingness to share tools

stress_responses.medium: Goes completely silent for hours; the prosthetic hand makes small repetitive adjustment movements
stress_responses.high: Leaves the workshop and walks the Grindstone Shore waterfront until he can think straight

contradictions: Values honesty above almost everything but has been lying about the arm for fifteen years
Attached to his machines with something approaching love but describes himself as having no sentimentality
habits: Full prosthetic inspection every Sunday, 0600, before anyone else is awake
Leaves machine oil in a small dish beside the diagnostic rig as an offering to the E.L.F. there
Never plays music while working — says it interferes with listening to the machines
breaking_points: Discovering that something he repaired was used to hurt someone

timeline.event: Born in Old Harbor to a Samoan-Dutch family with three generations in marine freight
Loses right arm; official record lists docking accident
Opens Tuiasosopo's garage after two years of rehabilitation and retraining
Reputation established; seven-year waitlist for vehicle work begins to develop
Installs olfactory sensor implant after losing a diagnostic job due to a fuel contamination he should have caught

carried_weapons: Street Custom 'Sunday School' Weaponized Religious Artifact
